messages:
Rachel: quick heads-up — during the quant4b bring-up I noticed ~1.7k records in the PrivateLabel ingest that are near-duplicates of our current golden anchors but with token masking applied. labelers are getting inconsistent guidance.

Kai: ouch, are these masked by deid pipeline or reingest? any example ids?

Rachel: looks like reingest + deid. sample ids: PL-4521, PL-4699, PL-4700. they match anchor hash but different tokenization because of masked emails/phones.

Marta: is this causing disagreement in the golden relabel run? saw a spike in disagreement rate earlier.

Rachel: yes — disagreement up ~12% on those buckets vs baseline. throwing more noise into evals for quant-int8 experiments.

Sam: can you run a fingerprint equality across normalized text (strip mask tokens) to confirm? I can patch sampler to exclude until we dedupe.

Rachel: running quick query now:

```sql
SELECT count(*) as cnt, normalized_fingerprint
FROM private_label.ingest
WHERE dataset_tag = 'private_v2'
GROUP BY normalized_fingerprint
HAVING cnt > 1
ORDER BY cnt desc
LIMIT 50;
```

Rachel: returns 1723 rows. attaching top5 hashes in thread.

LabelOps Bot: @LabelOps Bot detected 1723 likely duplicates across PrivateLabel -> recommended action: mark as "stitch-review" and pause auto-assign.

Marta: tagging @LabelOps to pause auto-assign, please. we need a small playbook: either stitch into existing anchors (preferred) or move to synthetic-holdout if deid changed semantics.

Kai: proposal: 1) dedupe by normalized_fingerprint, 2) create a mapping table private_to_anchor{private_id->anchor_id} for stitched ones, 3) add a flag `stitch_origin = "deid_reingest"`, 4) update labeler UI to show original anchor context.

Sam: for the short term I'll add a sampler rule: exclude `stitch_origin = 'deid_reingest'` from golden relabel runs and quant smoke until we finish mapping.

Rachel: also found a subtle tokenizer mismatch — masked phone tokens sometimes become multiple subword tokens leading to different kvcache behavior in the runtime. may bias quant results.

Marta: good catch. that can explain model perplexity bump on those examples. we should add a tokenizer-normalize step to the dedupe pipeline.

Kai: I'll open a tiny PR to curation-tools: `normalize_deid_for_fp` and add unit test with PL-4700.

Rachel: thanks. ETA?

Kai: I can do it today, review tomorrow morning.

Marta: ops requests: @oncall-bot can you apply a temporary tag `curation:hold-deid-stitch` to the 1.7k records so they don't hit staging evals?

oncall-bot: applied tag `curation:hold-deid-stitch` to 1723 records in private_v2.

Sam: I'll change the relabel job config: `exclude_tags: ["curation:hold-deid-stitch"]` and queue a quick smoke rerun after dedupe.

Marta: LabelOps -- plan to schedule a 1hr triage tomorrow 11:00 PT to decide stitch vs synthetic-holdout. agenda: mapping heuristics, UI changes, timeline.

LabelOps Bot: scheduled: "Deid Stitch Triage" • tomorrow 11:00 PT • invitees: Rachel, Kai, Marta, Sam, 2 label leads.

Rachel: one more thing — create a small golden patch set (50 cases) where we validate stitch decisions post-PR so quant/int8 benching isn't blocked. I can seed those.

Marta: yes please. pick high-variance examples. after PR + mapping we can rerun the quant smoke and compare regression delta.

Sam: ack — will hold the staging canary until the 50-case check is green.

Rachel: thanks all. I'll drop the example export & mapping sheet in the thread in ~30m. :thumbsup:
